1.web: I am a rose of Sharon, a lily of the valleys. Lover
1.asv: I am a rose of Sharon, A lily of the valleys.

2.web: As a lily among thorns, so is my love among the daughters. Beloved
2.asv: As a lily among thorns, So is my love among the daughters.

3.web: As the apple tree among the trees of the wood, so is my beloved among the sons. I sat down under his shadow with great delight, his fruit was sweet to my taste.
3.asv: As the apple-tree among the trees of the wood, So is my beloved among the sons. I sat down under his shadow with great delight, And his fruit was sweet to my taste.

4.web: He brought me to the banquet hall. His banner over me is love.
4.asv: He brought me to the banqueting-house, And his banner over me was love.

5.web: Strengthen me with raisins, refresh me with apples; For I am faint with love.
5.asv: Stay ye me with raisins, refresh me with apples; For I am sick from love.

6.web: His left hand is under my head. His right hand embraces me.
6.asv: His left handisunder my head, And his right hand doth embrace me.

7.web: I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, or by the hinds of the field, that you not stir up, nor awaken love, until it so desires.
7.asv: I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem, By the roes, or by the hinds of the field, That ye stir not up, nor awake my love, Until he please.

8.web: The voice of my beloved! Behold, he comes, leaping on the mountains, skipping on the hills.
8.asv: The voice of my beloved! behold, he cometh, Leaping upon the mountains, Skipping upon the hills.

9.web: My beloved is like a roe or a young deer. Behold, he stands behind our wall! He looks in at the windows. He glances through the lattice.
9.asv: My beloved is like a roe or a young hart: Behold, he standeth behind our wall; He looketh in at the windows; He glanceth through the lattice.

10.web: My beloved spoke, and said to me, “Rise up, my love, my beautiful one, and come away.
10.asv: My beloved spake, and said unto me, Rise up, my love, my fair one, and come away.

11.web: For, behold, the winter is past. The rain is over and gone.
11.asv: For, lo, the winter is past; The rain is over and gone;

12.web: The flowers appear on the earth. The time of the singing has come, and the voice of the turtledove is heard in our land.
12.asv: The flowers appear on the earth; The time of the singing of birds is come, And the voice of the turtle-dove is heard in our land;

13.web: The fig tree ripens her green figs. The vines are in blossom. They give out their fragrance. Arise, my love, my beautiful one, and come away.” Lover
13.asv: The fig-tree ripeneth her green figs, And the vines are in blossom; They give forth their fragrance. Arise, my love, my fair one, and come away.

14.web: My dove in the clefts of the rock, In the hiding places of the mountainside, Let me see your face. Let me hear your voice; for your voice is sweet, and your face is lovely.
14.asv: O my dove, that art in the clefts of the rock, In the covert of the steep place, Let me see thy countenance, Let me hear thy voice; For sweet is thy voice, and thy countenance is comely.

15.web: Catch for us the foxes, the little foxes that plunder the vineyards; for our vineyards are in blossom. Beloved
15.asv: Take us the foxes, the little foxes, That spoil the vineyards; For our vineyards are in blossom.

16.web: My beloved is mine, and I am his. He browses among the lilies.
16.asv: My beloved is mine, and I am his: He feedeth his flock among the lilies.

17.web: Until the day is cool, and the shadows flee away, turn, my beloved, and be like a roe or a young deer on the mountains of Bether.
17.asv: Until the day be cool, and the shadows flee away, Turn, my beloved, and be thou like a roe or a young hart Upon the mountains of Bether.
